title: When to Seek Immediate Emergency Medical Care
content: Students should immediately seek professional emergency medical care or call 911 (or campus emergency Ext: 911) if they experience any of the following serious symptoms: difficulty breathing or severe shortness of breath, persistent chest pain or pressure, sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, severe abdominal pain, high fever accompanied by a stiff neck, sudden confusion, or severe bleeding that won't stop.

title: First Aid and Immediate Health Crises
content: In case of a health crisis or emergency, call campus security or the 24/7 medical line (Ext: 911) immediately. While waiting for emergency responders, stay calm, keep the patient comfortable and still, do not give them anything to eat or drink, and do not attempt to move someone with a suspected neck or back injury unless they are in immediate danger.
